newsitem.title: KENYA: Foreigners buy at Nairobi bourse, market depressed.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners buy at Nairobi bourse, market depressed.

text.p: The Nairobi bourse still continued to attract foreign investors despite market sentiment being bearish, brokers and bourse officials said.
The index lost 8.75 points to stand at 3049.77. Turnover was posted at 8.437 million shillings traded on 373,743 shares from 19.381 million shillings traded on 501,858 shares on Wednesday.
Prices in key shares were on average unchanged -- with very marginal gains in Standard Chartered Bank and Kenya Breweries.
"The market sentiment is still pensive, in fact overall, the market is very quiet," a senior broker said.
Uchumi traded 12,500 shares at a steady 50, Nation Printers & Publishers traded at 106 from 108 while Standard Chartered gained 25 cents to 46.50 from 46.25.
Foreigners have maintained an active interest in the market in this period when the bourse has been depressed, buying big lots of shares in small lots spread over long periods.

"What you must realise is that what is good for me regarding the market might be bad for you. So even if the market is still depressed, foreigners will continue buying because this is a good time," a broker said. "Prices are low," he added.
Foreign investors bought 400 shares of Sasini Tea & Coffee, 800 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank and 16,300 shares of Kenya Breweries.
"Foreign investors are normally better informed than our local investors, they just don't buy just like that," he said.
"Even if the market is still low, on average current dividend yields are attractive and this keeps them in the market," another broker said.

Brokers said Kenya Breweries and Firestone East Africa traditionally have been traded by foreign investors, while Kenya Commercial Bank stands out currently among the financials on the percenption that its ownership is broader and management good.
